title: When can the police search you?
summary: A search of your body or belongings must have lawful authority and must be done in a way that respects your dignity.
body_plain: Your privacy is protected by the Constitution, and your dignity means you must not be searched in a degrading or inhuman way. While there are lawful procedures that permit searches in defined circumstances, a search cannot lawfully be arbitrary, humiliating, or used to extort you. A woman should ordinarily be searched by a female officer, and searches should be done as privately as the situation allows.
rights: Searches must have lawful authority and respect your privacy (s.37).
You must not be searched in a degrading or inhuman way (s.34(1)).
A woman should ordinarily be searched by a female officer.
do_list: Ask on what legal authority you are being searched.
Ask for privacy and, for a woman, a female officer.
Note who searched you, where, and any witnesses.
dont_list: Do not physically resist, but do not consent to a degrading search.
Do not let a search be used to extort money from you.
common_situations: An officer wants to search your pockets, bag, vehicle, or body at a checkpoint.
A search becomes unnecessarily exposing, humiliating, or more intrusive than expected.
Property is removed during a search without a clear record of what was taken.
words_to_use: What is the reason and legal authority for this search?
I do not consent, but I will not physically resist.
Please list any property you take and tell me how I can recover it.
if_violated: Record the location, time, officers, witnesses, stated reason, and manner of the search as soon as it is safe.
Make an inventory of missing or damaged property and preserve proof of ownership.
Seek medical help after an injurious or degrading search and obtain legal advice about complaint or redress.
